question: Why is the object of knowledge said to have a fourteen-fold nature?
premises: The object of knowledge is said to have a fourteen-fold nature.
Knower, means of knowing, and object of knowing are distinguished.
These three are proclaimed as one underlying reality.
inference: Therefore the fourteen-fold object of knowledge is taught within a framework where knower, means, and object are ultimately one.
uncertainties: The derivation of the number fourteen is not explicit in this verse alone.
plain_english: The object of knowledge is said to have a fourteen-fold nature. This is taught because knower, means of knowing, and knowable, though distinguished, are proclaimed as one.
